h: The Renewal of Shabbos Through Torah and Trust

p: In the zemiros for the night of Shabbos Kodesh we say:
The holiness of Shabbos is called "new faces,"
as in the matter mentioned in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory,
that is, the thing is renewed
And so it is stated in Tosafos (Kesubos 7b)
בְּשֵׁם אַגָּדַת מִזְמוֹר שִׁיר לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
in the name of the Aggadah on "A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day":
And it is stated in the Tikkunei Zohar
that it is the holy unification and union,
וְהָיָה כְּעֵץ שָׁתוּל עַל פַּלְגֵי מָיִם (תְּהִלִּים א, ג)
"And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water" (Tehillim 1:3),
דְּאִינּוּן פָּנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת (תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר כא, א)
For in the six days of the week
הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד
HaKadosh Baruch Hu renews each day continually
as it was at the beginning of Creation,
כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה ה׳ וְגוֹ׳
"For in six days Hashem made" etc.;
and this was through the Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וָאֶהְיֶה אֶצְלוֹ אָמוֹן (מִשְׁלֵי ח, ל)
as it says, "And I was with Him as a nursling" (Mishlei 8:30).
וּכְמוֹ כֵן בְּכָל שֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
And likewise in all the six weekdays
there is a renewal of the work of Creation
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu renews each day;
and this is the aspect of the six orders of Mishnah,
which is the root of Torah she'b'al peh.
וַעֲבוּר זֶה נִקְרָאִים תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בַּנָּאִים
And for this reason talmidei chachamim are called builders:
אַל תִּקְרָא בָּנַיִךְ אֶלָּא בּוֹנָיִךְ (בְּרָכוֹת סד, א)
And in the holiness of the Shabbos day
is included the very aspect of the renewal
כְּדְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב סג, ב)
as stated in the holy Zohar (II 63b):
"for it is the sum of all six days,
and from it they are blessed," etc.;
and Shabbos is the sum of the entire Torah.
And as stated in the Ohr HaChaim
עַל פָּסוּק וַיְכוּלּוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וְגוֹ׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, א)
on the pasuk "And the heavens were completed" etc. (Bereishis 2:1),
that through the holiness of Shabbos
longing for the root is added
and from it flows the strength
And this is the fondness and desire
and this is the root and source of renewal:
when one feels the sweetness of the taste
And as is alluded to in the pasuk
תּוֹרַת ה׳ תְּמִימָה וְגוֹ׳ (תְּהִלִּים יט, ח)
"The Torah of Hashem is perfect" etc. (Tehillim 19:8):
that allude to the six orders of Mishnah,
which corresponds to the holiness of Shabbos,
says, "More desirable than gold, than much fine gold,
And this is the matter of "new faces,"
they said: "He blessed it with the light of a person's face,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה מְאוֹר פָּנָיו שֶׁל אָדָם כּוּלֵּי
for the light of a person's face is not the same," etc.
And this is like what we find in Menachos (18a):
that words of Torah are so dear to you."
כִּי עַל יְדֵי שִׂמְחַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
For through the joy of words of Torah,
חָכְמַת אָדָם תָּאִיר פָּנָיו (קֹהֶלֶת ח, א)
"a man's wisdom lights up his face" (Koheles 8:1);
and as is written in Nedarim (49b)
that someone said to him, "teacher, drunk," etc.
And this is the light of the face of Shabbos,
through the renewal of joy in the heart:
"They shall rejoice in Your Kingship" etc.
And in Menachos there it concludes:
כָּל הַיּוֹם הִיא שִׂיחָתִי (תְּהִלִּים קיט, צז)
all day it is my conversation'" (Tehillim 119:97).
that in whatever a person is fixed
and cleaves to with the root of his soul,
in that is all his conversation,
And in the manner of what they said in Avos d'Rabbi Nosson
עַל אַל תַּרְבֶּה שִׂיחָה עִם הָאִישָּׁה
on "Do not converse excessively with a woman" (Avos 1:5),
that all their conversation is lewdness.
And about talmidei chachamim they said (Eruvin 54b):
"'Converse' — these are the masters of Talmud,
all of whose conversation is Torah."
And through the strength of love in the heart
זוֹכֶה לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁרָשׁ בּוֹ כָּל כָּךְ
one merits being so rooted in it
of nefesh and ruach are renewed,
whose dwelling is in the liver and heart.
And this is what it says about the future:
"And I will give you a new heart
And from the nefesh come all the bodily traits,
כִּי הַדָּם הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ (דְּבָרִים יב, כג)
and from it comes anger and its offshoots.
And opposite it in holiness is
the strength to conquer one's inclination
and to hate the enemies of Hashem
And likewise desire comes from the nefesh,
that affliction of the soul is
in refraining from the desire for eating
And opposite it in holiness is
love and yearning for words of Torah
And the ruach in the heart
is the fixing of the will in the heart,
from which are "the sources of life"
to be according to what was fixed in the will;
it turns" the organs of action.
they attributed the nefesh to the liver,
כִּי זִכְרוּתָא דְּדָמָא כַּבְדָּא (בְּכוֹרוֹת נה, א)
since "the essence of blood is the liver" (Bechoros 55a),
is in the revi'is of blood in the heart;
and its root in the liver
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק הָרוֹאֶה (בְּרָכוֹת סא, ב)
as is written in Perek HaRo'eh (Berachos 61b);
For in the heart is the ruach and the will,
and its beginning is in the blood drawn from the liver,
it is fixed to spread to the organs of action.
וְעַל כֵּן אָמַר שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ
And therefore it says there afterward,
"and you shall do that which" etc.,
וּמְסַיֵּים וְהָיִיתִי לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים (שָׁם לו, כז–כח)
and it concludes, "and I will be your God" (Yechezkel 36:27–28):
זֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ אַחַר כָּךְ
this is by their meriting afterward
which is a portion of God above.
And Shabbos is a semblance of the World to Come,
and it too has a renewal
a semblance of the World to Come.
And through the renewal of nefesh and ruach
there comes only an illumination of the face;
that there be truly new faces
this is from the aspect of new souls;
that is, the renewal of the face,
וְנִיכָּר בָּהּ כָּל כּוֹחוֹת שֶׁל הַנֶּפֶשׁ
in which all the powers of the soul are recognized,
as stated in the holy Zohar, Yisro,
עַל פָּסוּק וְאַתָּה תֶחֱזֶה (שְׁמוֹת יח, כא)
on the pasuk "And you shall discern" (Shemos 18:21);
that is, through feeling the taste
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה׳ (יְשַׁעְיָה נח, יד)
as it says, "Then you shall delight in Hashem" (Yeshayahu 58:14).
And this is cleaving to the root,
in the letter Alef, which is the Supernal Wonder,
which came about through the letters of the Torah,
which begins with the letter Beis of "Bereishis."
And as is known, the allusion
עַל רֹאשׁ דְּבָרְךָ אֱמֶ״ת (תְּהִלִּים קיט, קס)
on "The beginning of Your word is truth" (Tehillim 119:160),
that they are beginning, middle and end.
Alef is alluded to at the beginning of the Ten Commandments,
and this is the very source,
But in the revelation of Creation
it begins with the letter Beis, "Bereishis,"
and Torah she'bichsav ends with the letter Lamed;
and this is the whole of the revelation
from the beginning to the middle,
And this is the beginning of the six orders of Mishnah,
אָמְנָם הַגְּמָרָא מַתְחֶלֶת בְּאוֹת ת׳ תְּנָא
But the Gemara begins with the letter Tav, "Tana,"
and this is the whole of the root
from which one reaches up to the source
through feeling the reasons of the halachos;
וּמִזֶּה בָּאִים לְאָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה׳
and from this one comes to "Then you shall delight in Hashem,"

p: וְהָיָה כְּעֵץ שָׁתוּל עַל פַּלְגֵי מָיִם
"And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water,"
is at the beginning of the psalm of Tehillim
that begins "Fortunate is the man" etc.,
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said
that this psalm was dear to David,
וּמְסַיֵּים בְּאַשְׁרֵי כָּל חוֹסֵי בוֹ (תְּהִלִּים ב, יב)
and ends with "Fortunate are all who take refuge in Him" (Tehillim 2:12).
And it is stated about this in the Yerushalmi:
גַּם אִם לֹא הָלַךְ בַּעֲצַת רְשָׁעִים
even if he did not walk in the counsel of the wicked,
it is as if he walked in the counsel of the righteous;
שֶׁגַּם מִי שֶׁמּוֹנֵעַ אֶת עַצְמוֹ מֵעַוְלָה
that even one who restrains himself from wrong
is called one who walks in His ways.
the words of Chazal in Avodah Zarah (18b),
who said: "One might think he may doze off in sleep;
'But his desire is in the Torah of Hashem' etc."
that when one sat and did not commit a transgression
he is given reward like one who performs a mitzvah
that is, when a matter of transgression came his way
and he was saved from it.
Here too the main intent is
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר כִּי אִם בְּתוֹרַת ה׳ חֶפְצוֹ
as it says, "But his desire is in the Torah of Hashem,"
for it does not say "he walks in the Torah of Hashem";
that is, the ultimate aim of his effort in this,
from walking in the counsel of the wicked,
is that he merit that there shine upon him
and he knows in his soul
that by himself he has no power to be helped,
that the Torah will light up his way;
"who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked."
However, just as the 613 mitzvos of the Torah
so too, one opposite the other,
there are counsels on the opposite side,
from the side of the yetzer hara,
where it seems to a person
that it is advising him for his good;
like what our Sages, of blessed memory, said
בְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (חוּלִּין צא, א)
about Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him (Chullin 91a),
עַל וַיֵּאָבֵק אִישׁ עִמּוֹ (בְּרֵאשִׁית לב, כה)
on "And a man wrestled with him" (Bereishis 32:25):
he appeared to him like a talmid chacham,
וְעַל זֶה אֵין בְּכֹחַ הָאָדָם לְהִנָּצֵל
And from this a person has no power to be saved
except with the help of Hashem Yisbarach,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר כִּי ה׳ יִהְיֶה בְכִסְלֶךָ (מִשְׁלֵי ג, כו)
as it says, "For Hashem will be your confidence" (Mishlei 3:26)
in matters in which you are a fool.
אֲשֶׁר לֹא הָלַךְ בַּעֲצַת רְשָׁעִים וְגוֹ׳
"who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked" etc.,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיָּבֹא הֵלֶךְ וְגוֹ׳ (שְׁמוּאֵל ב יב, ד)
as it says, "And a wayfarer came" etc. (Shmuel II 12:4).
"But his desire is in the Torah of Hashem":
for this is the ultimate aim of his quest,
to illuminate his eyes with the light of His Torah, Yisbarach.
And through this it says immediately,
as in the words of Chazal (Avodah Zarah 19a).
וְהָיָה כְּעֵץ שָׁתוּל עַל פַּלְגֵי מָיִם
"And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water,"
as in the allusion mentioned above from the Tikkunim:
that this is the essence of the "new faces,"
the sweetness and pleasantness of the words of Torah.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה וְעָלֵיהוּ לֹא יִבּוֹל
And through this, "and its leaf shall not wither":
that even his conversation will be Torah;
that is, through feeling the sweetness
all his thought and conversation are in it,
as it says, "How I love Your Torah;
all day it is my conversation."
And the end of the psalm concludes
with "Fortunate are all who take refuge in Him":
that is, this is the ultimate purpose
only one who takes refuge in the Name of Hashem,

p: And it is stated in Maseches Soferim:
there are 175 parshiyos in the Torah
and they correspond to the years
of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him;
of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
"And You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Yisrael"
דְּהִנֵּה מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
For the middah of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
in an outpouring of great longing,
to give himself over with intense yearning
in order to publicize the holiness of His Name, Yisbarach;
and with him began the two thousand years of Torah,
alluded to in "Let there be light."
And therefore the parshiyos of the Torah are alluded
נֶגֶד כָּל שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
to correspond to all the years of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him.
And although at the beginning of his years
he did not yet recognize his Creator,
as our Sages, of blessed memory, said:
בֶּן ג׳ אוֹ בֶּן מ״ח הִכִּיר אֶת בּוֹרְאוֹ
at three or at forty-eight he recognized his Creator;
אָמְנָם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה לט, ח)
nevertheless our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bereishis Rabbah 39:8)
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to him,
"Yours is the dew of your youth" (Tehillim 110:3):
except that which comes forth from within darkness,
as in the matter of Creation:
וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים יְהִי אוֹר (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ב–ג)
"And God said, Let there be light" (Bereishis 1:2–3).
For he was clarified through his deeds
That is, after Yaakov was born from him,
אָמְנָם כְּשֶׁרָאָה יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
However, when Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him, saw
that dross had yet come forth from his father in Yishmael,
an aspect of alien yearning and kindness,
he began to conduct himself with the middah of constriction,
which is the aspect of yirah,
"Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination."
And when Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, came
and perceived that from this aspect too
this is the power of Esav,
that he has strength and might,
"his strength and the might of his hand"
he began to conduct his middos
to be, in all his matters, one who takes refuge in Him,
וּשְׁמָרַנִי בַּדֶּרֶךְ הַזֶּה וְגוֹ׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, כ)
and guard me on this way" etc. (Bereishis 28:20);
and at the end of his days he said,
מֵעוֹדִי עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה (שָׁם מח, טו)
from my beginning until this day" (Bereishis 48:15);
for this was clear before his eyes,
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם כֹּחַ וּתְנוּעָה מֵעוֹדוֹ
that he had no strength or movement ever,
only what flowed to him from above.
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן בְּחִינַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this too is the aspect of David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
whose strength is only in his mouth,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה (תְּהִלִּים קט, ד)
as he said, "And I am prayer" (Tehillim 109:4);
וְהַיְינוּ הַקּוֹל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב (בְּרֵאשִׁית כז, כב)
and this is "The voice is the voice of Yaakov" (Bereishis 27:22).
And therefore the psalms of Tehillim allude
נֶגֶד שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
to the years of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
כִּי זֶה עִיקַּר עִנְיַן כָּל סֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים
for this is the main theme of the entire Sefer Tehillim,
עַל פָּסוּק כִּי אִם בְּתוֹרַת ה׳ חֶפְצוֹ
on the pasuk "But his desire is in the Torah of Hashem,"
and it concludes, "Fortunate are all who take refuge in Him."
And this is the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos in time,
עַל פָּסוּק אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה׳
on the pasuk "Then you shall delight in Hashem,"
"and I will feed you the heritage of Yaakov your father";
וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת פֶּרֶק כָּל כִּתְבֵי)
and as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbos, Perek Kol Kisvei, 118a):
as it says, "And you shall spread out to the west and to the east."
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי בְּחִינָה שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק
That is, the aspect of Avraham and Yitzchak
avails only in the holiness of Eretz Yisrael,
לְךָ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ אֶתֵּן אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת
"To you and to your seed I will give this land";
and that is only when one guards his way in holiness.
אָמְנָם בְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נֶאֱמַר
But about Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, it says,
"And your seed shall be like the dust of the earth,
וּפָרַצְתָּ יָמָּה וָקֵדְמָה וְגוֹ׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, יד)
and you shall spread out to the west and to the east" etc. (Bereishis 28:14):
that although his children may reach
like the dust of the earth,
in exile in the land of the nations,
even there they will be clarified for good,
to spread out to the west and to the east,
עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
through the aspect of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him:
to take refuge in Him, Yisbarach,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִתְבָּרֵר הַכֹּל לְטוֹב
and through this everything will be clarified for good.
